_doc: Angelia overview. One entry per scene; sentences are cues. Numbers in words. Re-run narrate.py after any change.

en: Your project depends on hundreds of packages.
Each of them releases on its own schedule, somewhere else.
Angelia is a self-hosted release event bus.
It watches the registries for you, and turns every new version into one clean event.
It watches PyPI, npm, crates dot io, and the releases of GitHub and GitLab.
Fifty watches on the same package cost a single request.
Every new version is compared with the ones it already knows, in the package's own version scheme.
Policies decide what counts: pre-releases, ranges, the size of the bump, and a cooldown before anything moves.
The result is one CloudEvent, with a stable id, the bump, and a package URL.
Every consumer reads the same shape.
Angelia delivers it to signed webhooks, GitHub Actions, and chat.
Consumers without a public address pull it from a cursor, and AI agents ask through MCP.
Deliveries that fail are retried, then kept for replay.
It is one binary, with SQLite or Postgres.
With Docker, it runs in a few minutes.
Angelia. Hear about every release, before your users do.
